newsitem.title: UK: Securicor dips after H1 profit decline.
newsitem.headline: Securicor dips after H1 profit decline.

text.p: Shares in Securicor Plc nudged lower in early trade on Thursday after the security-to-mobile phones group posted a sharp drop in pre-tax profit for the first half ended March 31.
The stock was down 4p at 284-1/2 by 0721 GMT in volume of 18,500 shares.
Pre-tax profit before exceptional items and interest charges dipped to 56.1 million stg from 57.7 million, yet after charges pre-tax profit tumbled to 19.1 million stg from 47.6 million.
Analyst expectations had been in a range between 45 million stg and 55 million.
SocGen analyst John Tysoe described the results as not particularly impressive, though the profit figures were heavily distorted by one-off factors.
"One wonders whether Securicor will ever attain the type of profitability that seems to come naturally to Vodafone," Tysoe said.
He added that the outlook for the stock could be altered by any sign of an easing in the government block on selling its stake in Celltech to partner British Telecommunications Plc.

In a statement, chairman Sir Neil Macfarlane said Securicor's results at the trading level reflected a strong recovery in security operations, a good performance in distribution and an improved contribution from Cellnet.
However, these were offset by losses in the company's Cellular Services unit and development costs in its U.S. mobile radio network Intek.

MacFarlane said losses would continue in Securicor Cellular Services and that Intek costs would continue to affect the results, but said he had "confidence in the longer-term performance of communications."
